kept.excerpt: The FIFA Young Player Award will be presented to the best young player (born on or after 1 January 2005) in the final competition, as selected by the FIFA Technical Study Group. Yamal is still only 18 and is going into the World Cup after a season with 42 goal contributions in 45 appearances for Barcelona. FIFA's candidate preview also profiles Desire Doue, Joao Neves, Endrick, Pau Cubarsi, Warren Zaire-Emery, Arda Guler, Antonio Nusa, Yan Diomande, Ibrahim Maza and Kenan Yildiz.
kept.relevance: Establishes the official eligibility and selection process, identifies Yamal as a candidate and documents the competing field before the tournament.

kept.excerpt: Spain's coach backed Lamine Yamal ahead of Monday's World Cup last-16 showdown with Portugal, saying he loves these kinds of games. The 18-year-old Barcelona attacker did not score but turned in an eye-catching display in Spain's 3-0 win over Austria in the last 32. Spain had followed an opening 0-0 draw against Cape Verde with three consecutive wins without conceding a goal.
kept.relevance: Provides a recent dated assessment of Yamal's tournament form and Spain's progress immediately before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Spain have gone through to the quarter-finals.
kept.relevance: Confirms that Spain remained in contention after its last-16 match on the experiment date, preserving Yamal's opportunity to play further knockout matches.

kept.excerpt: In Atlanta, Lamine Yamal scored his first World Cup goal, opening the scoring in Spain's 4-0 win over Saudi Arabia at the age of 18 years and 343 days. He played the opening 45 minutes and scored by sliding in at the far post to finish Mikel Oyarzabal's cross.
kept.relevance: Documents Yamal's first goal and playing time during the tournament using a dated official club report.

kept.excerpt: Spain winger Lamine Yamal was fit and ready to come off the bench in his side's opening World Cup game, but manager Luis de la Fuente said his entrance would depend on how the match with Cape Verde progressed. Yamal had not played since April because of groin issues and a hamstring injury, and had missed Spain's recent friendlies.
kept.relevance: Records the injury and limited initial availability that affected Yamal's preparation and early tournament participation.

kept.excerpt: Pau Cubarsi's date of birth is 22 January 2007 and his position is centre-back. Despite having only turned 19 a few months earlier, he had accumulated over 135 appearances for Barcelona. Cubarsi completed the full 90 minutes in three of Spain's final four qualifiers for the 2026 World Cup.
kept.relevance: Documents the age eligibility, experience and national-team role of a same-team competitor identified in FIFA's pre-tournament candidate coverage.

kept.excerpt: UEFA's team of technical observers named Lamine Yamal EURO 2024 Young Player of the Tournament. He recorded one goal, four assists and 32 dribbles, with the latter two totals both tournament highs. Yamal appeared in all seven of Spain's games, starting six, and assisted Nico Williams's opening goal in the final.
kept.relevance: Provides official evidence of Yamal's previous ability to earn a major international tournament's young-player award through creativity and sustained participation.

kept.excerpt: Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez was crowned Young Player of the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022. Fernandez also became a world champion as Argentina beat France 4-2 on penalties after a 3-3 draw. The 21-year-old scored against Mexico in Argentina's 2-0 group-stage victory.
kept.relevance: Supplies a dated historical precedent showing that the award can go to a midfielder with a modest goal tally on a successful team.
